cells.tense: You know what matters and the pen is in your hand, moving at its own pace.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing this week that deserves your full attention and give it that — not the leftover hour, the good one.
cells.core:
You know what matters before you can explain why. Something gets your attention and the matter resolves itself before you've built a case for it. Right now that's working, and so is what sits under it: what you want and what you do are moving in the same direction. You're not pushing the river. You picked the right thing to attend to and the attending carries you.

It's worth noticing, because a balance like this feeds what comes next, and what comes next is bigger than what you've already imagined. Take one thing this week and give it your whole attention, not the tired end of the day. Let the doing be its own reward for once, instead of the proof you needed something.

cells.tense: You're already attending to next week, and you haven't finished arriving in this one.
cells.ask: Write down what you're watching for that hasn't happened yet, then cross out every line you can do nothing about today.
cells.core:
Your attention has started sorting things that haven't arrived. The instinct is good — that's not the problem — but it's running ahead of the moment, sifting threats and outcomes that aren't here yet. You check the same situation twice, three times, looking for the detail that will finally let you rest. A quiet readiness has turned into vigilance, and it's being spent on days that haven't opened.

What's underneath is still sound: you can feel which way to move, and when you trust that instead of auditing it, the direction holds. It's the pre-checking that's wearing you down. So take the list of what you're braced for and cross off what today can't touch. What's left is the short, real list — and your own sense of it can carry that one without the rehearsal.

cells.tense: You saw what mattered back when it was in front of you, and you're still standing at that door.
cells.ask: Pick one thing already on your plate and write the single next step for it, then do that step before you judge whether it was right.
cells.core:
There's something you saw plainly, the way you do — and you haven't started. That way of seeing hasn't left you; what stopped is the moving. Days pass and the thing sits where it was, and from where you're standing it's starting to look as if you lost the knack entirely.

You didn't. What's actually low is fuel, not judgment, and fuel comes back through small real steps rather than waiting to feel ready. Put one next step on paper and take it before you decide what it means. The door you're standing at is already behind you — the step forward is the whole test, and you've passed harder ones.

cells.tense: You're picking what gets your attention right now, and calling it something that happens by itself.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, that you chose to spend today the way you spent it — name the one thing you gave your attention to.
cells.core:
Things come at you all day and you let some through and wave the rest past, and that picking is yours — it runs the day whether you claim it or not. The words you use for it are different, though. You talk as if the day decided itself, as if the important things surfaced on their own and you happened to be there when they did.

They didn't surface by themselves. You noticed them. When nothing gets called chosen, the day starts to feel like drift, and drift is harder to trust — especially from someone whose whole gift is knowing what to attend to. So say it once, out loud: that one, today, on purpose. The claim and the picking are the same act.
cells.sheetLine: You're already picking what matters. Only you're not the one saying so.
